Package com.csse3200.game.components.pausemenu

Class PauseMenuFactory

java.lang.Object
com.csse3200.game.components.pausemenu.PauseMenuFactory
public final class PauseMenuFactory extends Object
Assembles the in-game pause menu cluster — PauseMenuDisplay, PauseMenuInput, PauseMenuActions and an in-place SaveLoadPanel overlay — and attaches it to a screen's UI entity, so each gameplay screen wires the pause menu with a single call.

It registers a GamePauseService if the screen didn't, and loads the shared menu textures the styled pause menu / save panel need.

  • Method Details

    • attach

      public static SaveLoadPanel attach(Entity uiEntity, GdxGame game)
      Adds the pause menu (and its save/load overlay) to uiEntity. Call before the screen registers the entity; then call SaveLoadPanel.hide() on the returned panel once the entity has been created, so the save overlay starts hidden.
      Parameters:
      uiEntity - the screen's UI entity to attach to
      game - the running game, used for run state and screen navigation
      Returns:
      the save/load panel, so the caller can hide it after the entity is created

    • attach

      public static SaveLoadPanel attach(Entity uiEntity, GdxGame game, int pauseButtonAlign)
      As attach(Entity, GdxGame), but places the on-screen pause button in the given corner (an Align constant) so each screen can keep it clear of its own HUD.

    • attach

      public static SaveLoadPanel attach(Entity uiEntity, GdxGame game, int pauseButtonAlign, float pauseButtonEdgePad)
      As above, but also insets the pause button from the screen edges, to nudge it clear of nearby HUD (e.g. beside the Map's own Main Menu button).

    • attachWithoutButton

      public static SaveLoadPanel attachWithoutButton(Entity uiEntity, GdxGame game)
      Attaches the pause menu with Escape-only access (no on-screen pause button) — for screens where the button doesn't fit the HUD, e.g. the map.
